question: Should OpenClaw expose a public exec approval timeout override, and if so what canonical key, bounds, units, and environment precedence should it use?
rationale: The request adds public configuration around a host-exec authorization window, and the current code does not establish the product/security contract for operator-controlled approval expiry.

options.title: Approve bounded core config
options.body: Add one canonical timeout key with conservative min/max validation, documented precedence, and tests covering both default and configured approval windows.

options.title: Keep fixed timeout
options.body: Leave the 30-minute default as the product contract and close duplicate timeout-knob requests after explaining that approval-window tuning is intentionally not configurable.

options.title: Defer to narrower mitigations
options.body: Avoid a general timeout knob for now and address only specific no-route, stale-approval, or notification problems as separate bugs.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded core config
recommendation.body: Add one canonical timeout key with conservative min/max validation, documented precedence, and tests covering both default and configured approval windows.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared timeout and core exec approval request path history point most strongly to this owner for the config/security decision.
